Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: paired_population: 'Every arm scored on identical events' — 4848 events in the shared window; every arm has seen all of them.
findings.problem: Seeing an event is not being scored on it. The arena's own screen_n values differ across arms on the same shared stream: hold-12h 1563, control/placebo/sl-5pct 1560, tp-7pct 1556, vol-4x 874, entry-8pct 498. Arms whose parameter changes the detection set (entry-8pct, vol-4x) are scored on a strict subset, so any arm-vs-arm delta involving them is not paired and the green checkbox does not establish what its title claims.

Both arms report a delta of exactly 0.0pp against control while their own screen_wr values differ from control's screen_wr of 50.128 (entry-8pct 51.807, vol-4x 51.487). Only placebo, at an identical 50.128, has earned a 0.0pp delta. The dWR field is evidently being zeroed rather than computed for arms with non-matching populations, yet it is displayed in the same column as hold-12h's 3.27pp and sl-5pct's 5.26pp — the headline comparison stat is silently not comparable across rows.

findings.claim: bonferroni_monotonic: 'Corrected bar counts every question asked' — lifetime tests=6, pre-registered hypotheses=6, alpha=0.00833.
findings.problem: The count of 6 does not cover questions already asked and answered. L-sl-entry-anchor records a completed screen kill on n=1474 with paired p=9.18e-41 evaluated against alpha=0.01250 — a different, looser correction than 0.00833 — and eight further retired/screen arms carry their own lockfile verdicts. A bar that has already been applied at two different levels within this context is not monotonic, and the checkbox is green on a self-reported hypothesis count rather than on the tests visible in the data.

findings.claim: Seven arms are listed as [running/confirm], including entry-8pct.
findings.problem: Confirm was planned at n=600, and the context states explicitly that a fixed n=100 detects only very large effects. The largest live_n in the arena is 26 (hold-12h); entry-8pct is at live_n=5 with a negative screen_ev of -0.035 and declined=79. Nothing in the confirm stage yet has live evidence at any usable sample size, so every number now differentiating these arms — including the 3.27pp and 5.26pp headline deltas — comes from the backfill screen, which the backfill_cannot_promote check itself says may not promote.

findings.claim: 'MECHANISM CLASSES (one per running arm — diversity is enforced in code)'.
findings.problem: The running set violates the stated one-per-class rule twice: control and entry-8pct are both class=entry_trigger, and placebo and vol-4x are both class=liquidity_filter. Control, which changes nothing (changed={}), is also occupying an entry_trigger slot it does not test. Either the enforcement does not apply to control and placebo — which is undocumented here — or the diversity claim is not actually enforced.

findings.claim: 'measured ghost arrival = 24.9 control trades/day' in STATISTICAL REALITY.
findings.problem: Three other control-arrival baselines appear elsewhere in the same context, each stated as measured and each used to size a confirm horizon: 25.6 trades/day in L-dedup-0h, 25.2 in L-minprice-1, and 25.0 in L-pump-window-1h. Four different values for the same quantity are quoted without the n or window behind any of them, so the time-to-n=600 arguments built on them are not reproducible from this data.
